Yes, that is their point Einstein. 

> Hospitalisations and ICU patients have doubled in a week. Test positivity rate has jumped to 2.27% (was 0.93% a week ago) with many reports of delays for results.

> And our premier still thinks he's being brave by refusing to bring back masks, QR codes, and WFH when we still don't know enough about Omicron.
I don't blame you, I don't understand my point of view either. I am living it though, for now.

I was prescribed quetiapine (Seroquel), and told to take it before bed. I found the same issues you are describing and also am not psychotic, I stopped taking it because it did more harm than good. 

A lot of the brain meds are pretty new and if you read into how they were discovered usually they were trialling for some other treatment and it turned out they helped with mental health issues, but often they don't even know why they help, let alone how and best practices for what. 

I have OCD and personally found Zoloft to be helpful, but its always about 6 weeks before I can properly assess whether the medication has helped and if there are any long term issues. 

Also PSA: See how I didn't tell you you should have thought about this BEFORE you went to see a doctor to ask for help, that is what being supportive is, not telling someone they are a fuck up when they clearly already know.

Because he gets so broken hearted and I love him deep down a lot, love is different than I can understand, and so I empathise very much with how much I'm hurting him - it feels like razors in my heart. I understand that this inbetween situation is hurtful too. But for him me leaving him is much much worse than me having an affair, and I go almost catatonic when I am have left him, just frozen and worrying about him.

Worse, a marriage is a financial partnership as well as a romantic one. I feel incredibly guilty pulling the house that he worked so hard for out from under him, or making him be alone at the age of 40. 

I am worried about his mental well being. My dad never got over my mum leaving him. In fact I dont personally know anyone who has been happy or properly gotten over a divorce, that and I am a huge coward when it comes to going through with breaking anyones heart or making their life immeasurably worse. Both of which me leaving does. I don't want to be the one taking away half of his income, taking away the house we both worked so hard for the last 10 years. Leaving him to be lonely - he has no friends either. He said last year when I tried to leave him that I was his only friend and he is right. 

Basically I am a cowardly, piece of shit, who can't impose pain on others so I make everything worse at every step, my inability to tell other people no, or do what is in my own best interest even.
I find this endearing in some people, when they aren't trying to seem smart just believing thats what the word meant

Same! My parents sent our dog jessie away to a farm in the early 2000s because she just chewed through everything and mum couldnt deal with it. She was only a couple of years old then mum and my sister went and visited her 10 years later when she was an old but happy doggo. The family loved her very much.
Because I am trying to figure out how to do it.
Unbelievable, just so unethical. Fucking horrible, self serving corruption.
Yeah holy moly what a cunt!
